title: Oracle's Wisconsin AI data center hits a Wisconsin power line roadblock
key_facts: On 7 Aug 2026 Wisconsin's Public Service Commission voted unanimously to revoke a completeness approval it had granted to American Transmission Co. (ATC) for the line serving Oracle's 1.3 GW Port Washington campus (Project Lighthouse).
ATC had filed or refiled 564 application documents; the chair called it a 'moving-target application'.
Startup Fortune calls it a first in the commission's 95-year history.
Research firm Aterio (30 Sep report): base case of 180 days for review puts partial power around December 2027 and full 1.3 GW around October 2028; worst case 360 days, April 2029.
Oracle told customers the site would start serving in the second half of 2027.
The reworked line may cost $2.48 to $2.72 billion; Oracle shares fell about 1.8% on the unconfirmed delay report, per Yahoo Finance.
quote_evidence: On August 7, Wisconsin's Public Service Commission did something it had never done in its 95-year history: it voted unanimously to revoke a completeness determination it had already granted.
Oracle has told customers it expects the Wisconsin site to begin serving them in the second half of 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Power-line paperwork, not chips, may delay one of Oracle's biggest AI sites.
notes: Startup Fortune is an aggregator-style outlet; its facts rest on the PSC, Aterio, Urban Milwaukee, Yahoo Finance and TMJ4, none opened here. Aterio dates are projections.
